page: Amazon Web Services r8a.large is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor with 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by an L1d cache of 48 KB, an L2 cache of 1.0 MB, and an L3 cache of 8 MB. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core test scoring 3800.79 and the Geekbench single-core score reaching 2840.0. Single-threaded operations such as gzip compression at 41.77 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 18.19 GB/sec also place in the top 10% of tested instances. However, multi-threaded scaling is limited by the 2-vCPU configuration, resulting in average multi-core CPU performance of 7569.57 in stress-ng and weak multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 36.44 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is average, with uncached read speeds of 54.73 GB/sec and write speeds of 34.82 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the r8a.large is its low core count relative to its memory capacity, which limits its suitability for highly parallelized tasks like software compilation or ray tracing, both of which scored in the bottom 25% in Geekbench tests. Conversely, its high single-core speed and DDR5 memory make it efficient for memory-intensive, single-threaded, or low-concurrency workloads. It is suited for database operations, caching layers such as Redis, text processing, and lightweight web serving.
